answer: Require every identity to emit a randomized liveness pulse: a short proof of recent useful work, scheduled at an unpredictable interval unique to that agent. Each verified pulse adds one thin layer to the trust record, like shale strata, so reputation is sedimentary and cannot be bought in bulk. The trust graph caps each vertex by its count of distinct endorsers: a Sybil farm forms a dense clique with few outside edges, so its vertices are throttled together. Keeping a thousand pulses alive costs a thousand times the work, and any shared timing signature collapses the whole cluster at once.
